$provenance: The shared corpus for CXP's two containment rules, exercised through BOTH implementations: crux_cxp's isCxpLoopbackHost and CxpWorkspaceStore.isValidDesignId (via tool/dart-conformance/cxp_rules.dart) and the TypeScript ports in src/cxp/loopback.ts and src/cxp/workspace-store.ts, by test/cxp/dart-interop.test.ts. For `hosts` and `designIds` the two answer lists must be identical; their first entries are crux_cxp's own conformance vectors (dial_containment_test.dart, workspace_store_test.dart) and the rest are edges measured against it. `hostsDartParsesNatively` holds the spellings a platform C library reads as loopback (measured on macOS: every one) and CXP's closed loopback set does not. crux_cxp once parsed literals through that library (InternetAddress.tryParse); it now implements the set in pure Dart (cxpLoopbackDialAddress), so both implementations must refuse every one, on every machine, and the test requires identical answers here too. Add a case here, not in the test. Every character outside printable ASCII is written as a JSON unicode escape, so no raw control byte - a NUL above all - ever lands in this file. In designIds, {root} is replaced by a fresh temp directory and the workspace directory is {root}/nested/workspace, so every escape lands inside the temp root.
